summary: Mostly not. ADX(14) crossing up 25, above 25 or 40, below 20 or crossing down through 20 did the same as random entries on 1h, 4h and daily, pooled across BTC, ETH and SOL. The result that holds up is in downtrends: after DMI(14) +DI crossed above −DI on 4h and daily, and after ADX(14) crossed down through 20 on 4h, price beat random entries taken in the same regime.

verdicts.use: Catching a new trend (ADX crosses up 25)
verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h, 4h and daily. It was also the same as random in uptrends and in downtrends.

verdicts.use: Riding a strong trend (ADX above 25 or 40)
verdicts.text: Same as random pooled on every timeframe. ADX(14) above 40 on 1h beat random only while the pair closed above its 200-day SMA.

verdicts.use: Trading a quiet market (ADX below 20 or crossing down 20)
verdicts.text: Same as random pooled. On 4h the cross down through 20 beat random in downtrends and did worse in uptrends, so the pooled figure hides two opposite results.
Beat random on 1h at 20 candles only, carried by SOL. On 4h and daily it was the same as random pooled, but it beat random in downtrends.
Beat random on daily, but only because of one stretch between Nov 7, 2020 and Jun 15, 2021. Same as random on 1h and 4h.

verdicts.use: Shorting a bearish DMI cross (+DI crosses below −DI)
verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h, 4h and daily.

notes: On 1h, ADX(14) crossing up through 25 gave 2,816 entries in 2,350 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.09% ahead of random entries, inside the luck band. Holding while ADX(14) stayed above 25 enters on far more candles and lands in the same place, 0.02% ahead.

ADX(14) above 40 on 1h splits by regime. In uptrends it beat random by 0.25%, held without its strongest stretch, the May 19–20, 2021 crash, and showed at 10 and 20 candles but not at 50 or 100. In downtrends it was 0.13% behind, the same as random. On 4h the uptrend result of 0.83% rests on one stretch between Aug 30 and Sep 8, 2021, and without it the result is chance.

ADX(14) crossing down through 20 on 4h was the same as random pooled, at 0.26% behind. In downtrends it beat random by 0.68%, held without its strongest stretch on Oct 19–25, 2022, and showed at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles. In uptrends it was 0.83% worse than random, but that rests on signals on Jan 3–4, 2022 and shows at 20 candles only.

The DMI(14) cross of +DI above −DI shows the same downtrend shape. In downtrends it beat random by 0.53% on 4h and by 4.64% on daily, and each held without its strongest stretch. The 4h result shows at 10 and 20 candles, the daily one at 10, 20 and 50. In uptrends it was the same as random, at 0.32% behind on 4h and 0.27% ahead on daily.

On 1h the same cross was 0.11% ahead pooled, but only at 20 candles, so it counts as fragile. SOL carried it at 0.24%, while BTC sat at 0.01%. On daily, +DI staying above −DI was 3.04% ahead, but that rests on 179 entries between Nov 7, 2020 and Jun 15, 2021, and without them the result is chance.

For a long DCA bot, ADX levels alone did not change where price went on these pairs, so the DCA orders and take profit do the work. The data does show a shape in downtrends: a +DI cross above −DI on 4h or daily, or ADX(14) dropping back below 20 on 4h, came before rebounds that beat random. Test it as a filter beside a condition that marks the downtrend, such as price below the 200-day SMA, not as the bot's only start condition. A short bot that opens on a bearish DMI cross got nothing from it, so leaving that condition out costs nothing.
